glosses.notes: Can mean ensuring something is protected or has the support it needs, and it can also refer to that protection itself.

examples.sentence: 学校在安排活动路线的时候，不只是看风景好不好，还得先确认路上的通信和医疗条件能不能保障大家的安全。
这个平台想长期留住用户，光靠低价还不够，更重要的是拿出稳定服务来保障大家最在意的个人信息安全。
新来的经理上任以后先补上夜班休息制度，因为他觉得连基本健康都保障不了，谈效率就没有意义了。

example_translations.translation: When the school planned the activity route, it did not just look at whether the scenery was good; it first had to confirm whether communication and medical conditions on the way could ensure everyone's safety.
If this platform wants to keep users for the long term, low prices alone are not enough; what matters more is stable service that safeguards the personal information people care about most.
After the new manager took over, he first added a night-shift rest system, because he felt that if even basic health could not be protected, talking about efficiency was meaningless.

glosses.notes: Used when something suddenly bursts or explodes, often with a loud sound.

examples.sentence: 演出刚结束，后台有人把没关好的气瓶搬到门口时突然爆了，吓得等车的人全都回头看。
天太热的时候，那辆车上的旧轮子忽然爆了，保安赶紧拉开围栏，提醒路人别靠近。
厨房里那只装得太满的盒子被人一碰就爆开了，里面的调料撒得到处都是，旁边排队买饭的人都往后退了一步。

example_translations.translation: Just after the performance ended, someone backstage was moving an unsealed gas cylinder to the doorway when it suddenly exploded, making the people waiting for rides all turn around.
When the weather got too hot, one of the old wheels on that car suddenly burst, and the security guard quickly pulled open the barrier and warned passersby not to come close.
The overfilled box in the kitchen burst open the moment someone brushed against it, spilling seasoning everywhere and making the people lined up for food step back.

glosses.notes: Used for something intense suddenly erupting, such as conflict, fire, illness, or emotion.

examples.sentence: 会场外本来只是两个人小声争论，后来因为排队顺序的问题突然爆发争吵，工作人员只好先暂停入场。
那片山火在半夜突然爆发以后，周围几个村子的广播不停提醒居民按路线往安全地带离开。
长期压着不说的压力一旦爆发出来，往往就不是一件小事，所以老师才一直劝他早点找人谈一谈。

example_translations.translation: Outside the venue, what began as a quiet argument between two people suddenly broke into open quarrelling over the line order, so the staff had to pause entry first.
After the wildfire suddenly broke out in the middle of the night, broadcasts in several surrounding villages kept reminding residents to follow the route toward a safe area.
Once pressure that has been held in for a long time suddenly flares up, it is usually no small matter, which is why the teacher kept urging him to find someone to talk to sooner.

glosses.notes: A collective word for newspapers and magazines, especially as published media.

examples.sentence: 车站旁边那家老书店虽然地方不大，每天清早都有不少退休老人进去翻当天刚到的报刊。
图书馆把近十年的地方报刊都整理成电子资料以后，做城市研究的人查消息方便了很多。
他去社区服务中心做志愿者时，顺手把服务台上没人拿走的报刊按日期排好，免得下午又堆成一团。

example_translations.translation: That old bookstore beside the station is not large, but every early morning quite a few retired people still go in to leaf through the newspapers and magazines that just arrived.
After the library organized local newspapers and magazines from the last ten years into digital materials, people studying the city found it much easier to look up information.
While volunteering at the community service center, he casually arranged the newspapers and magazines left on the service counter by date so they would not pile up again in the afternoon.

glosses.notes: Refers to physical or other harmful force used to control, attack, or intimidate.

examples.sentence: 电影虽然没有直接拍出暴力场面，那种让人紧张的气氛已经让不少观众半路出去透气。
学校开家长会的时候反复强调，有冲突的时候不能用暴力解决问题，孩子先学会求助才更重要。
社区最近在地铁口办了一个展览，提醒大家别把伤人的话和网络攻击当成小事，因为那也是一种暴力。

example_translations.translation: Although the film never directly showed scenes of violence, the tense atmosphere alone was enough to make many viewers step outside midway for air.
At the parent meeting, the school repeatedly stressed that conflicts should not be solved with violence, and that it is more important for children to learn to ask for help.
The community recently set up an exhibit at the subway entrance reminding everyone not to treat hurtful speech and online attacks as small matters, because those too are a form of violence.

glosses.notes: Used when something hidden, private, or previously unnoticed gets uncovered.

examples.sentence: 那张没有处理的照片一传出去，就把住址和车牌一起暴露了，平台连夜联系上传的人删掉原图。
问题不是一天出现的，只是这次停电把设备长期没人维护的情况一下子暴露得很明显。
他说话看起来一直很冷静，一提到那次合作失败，脸上的不服气还是立刻暴露出来了。

example_translations.translation: As soon as that unedited photo was shared, it exposed the address and license plate together, and the platform contacted the uploader overnight to delete the original image.
The problem did not appear in a single day; this blackout simply made it very obvious that the equipment had gone without maintenance for a long time.
He sounded calm the whole time, but the moment that failed collaboration came up, the resentment on his face immediately showed.

glosses.notes: The office or organization that edits and publishes a newspaper.

examples.sentence: 她去报社实习的第一周，每天最紧张的不是写文章，而是怕自己把采访录音的时间和地点记错。
暴雨那天不少路都封了，报社还是临时派车把记者送到现场，因为第二天一早要印的报纸必须连夜做完。
老城区那栋旧楼以前是报社，后来改成博物馆以后，墙上还留着当年排版室的照片和说明。

example_translations.translation: In her first week interning at the newspaper office, what made her most nervous was not writing articles but worrying that she might record the wrong time and place of an interview.
Even though many roads were closed that day because of heavy rain, the newspaper office still sent a car to take reporters to the scene, because the next morning's paper had to be finished overnight.
That old building in the old district used to be a newspaper office, and after it was turned into a museum, photos and descriptions of the old layout room were still left on the walls.

glosses.notes: Usually refers to an object or substance exploding, and it can also name the blast itself.

examples.sentence: 实验室的人后来反复回看录像，才发现那只旧瓶子是因为温度太高才突然爆炸，根本不是谁碰倒的。
周围的人听见仓库里先有一点响，还没反应过来，后面更大的爆炸就已经让窗子一直在动了。
活动刚开始时，主持人就提醒家长别让孩子把气球拿到灯旁边，因为一受热就可能突然爆炸，把前排的人都吓一跳。

example_translations.translation: After repeatedly rewatching the footage, the lab staff realized that the old bottle had exploded because the temperature was too high, not because anyone had knocked it over.
People nearby heard a small sound from the warehouse first and had not even reacted yet when a larger explosion was already making the windows keep shaking.
As soon as the event began, the host reminded parents not to let children hold balloons near the lights, because once heated they could suddenly explode and startle everyone in the front rows.

glosses.notes: Describes expecting the worst or seeing little hope in a situation.

examples.sentence: 项目刚碰到一点麻烦他就特别悲观，连还没试过的办法也先说没用，弄得整个会议气氛越来越低。
医生已经说明恢复机会还在，家里最小的弟弟一听见要做长期治疗就变得很悲观，谁劝都听不进去。
导演不想把故事拍得太悲观，所以结尾虽然没有奇迹，也让那家人看见了慢慢往前走的可能。

example_translations.translation: The moment the project hit a small problem, he became deeply pessimistic and dismissed even untried solutions, dragging the mood of the whole meeting down.

The doctor had already explained that there was still a chance of recovery, but the youngest brother in the family became very pessimistic as soon as he heard it would require long-term treatment and would not listen to anyone.
The director did not want the story to feel too gloomy, so although the ending had no miracle, it still let that family see a way to keep moving forward slowly.

glosses.notes: Can mean a tragic event in real life or a tragedy in literature or drama.

examples.sentence: 那场山路事故后来被很多人当成悲剧来谈，不只是因为有人受伤，更因为原本完全可以提前避免。
小说前半段写得很平静，看到最后大家才发现，作者早就在许多小细节里埋好了悲剧的影子。
老师说把一次失败说成悲剧没有帮助，真正该做的是弄清楚哪里出错，别让同样的事再发生。

example_translations.translation: That mountain-road accident was later spoken of as a tragedy, not only because people were hurt, but even more because it could have been prevented in advance.
The first half of the novel feels calm, but by the end everyone realizes that the author had already planted the shadow of tragedy in many small details.
The teacher said it does not help to call one failure a tragedy; what matters is finding out what went wrong so the same thing does not happen again.

glosses.notes: Describes deep sadness, whether in a person's mood, expression, or the feeling of a work.

examples.sentence: 她听完整段录音以后没有马上哭，只是坐在窗边很久都不说话，那种安静反而让人更觉得悲伤。
送别会结束以后，大家本来想说点轻松的话，一看见空着的座位，刚压下去的悲伤又全上来了。
这首曲子一开始并不特别慢，越往后听越悲伤，像是在把一个人不愿意说出口的心事慢慢拉长。

example_translations.translation: After listening to the whole recording, she did not cry right away; she just sat by the window in silence for a long time, and that quiet somehow felt even sadder.
After the farewell gathering ended, everyone wanted to say something light, but the moment they saw the empty seat, the sadness they had just pushed down came flooding back.
This piece does not begin especially slowly, but the farther it goes, the sadder it sounds, as if it were slowly stretching out thoughts someone does not want to say aloud.

glosses.notes: Usually refers to the North Pole or the polar region around it.

examples.sentence: 讲到北极的时候，老师没有先放地图，而是先问大家如果半年看不见太阳，生活会变成什么样。
关于北极考察的那段视频拍得很安静，只有风和脚下的声音，却让人一直移不开眼。
他小时候一直以为北极只是课本上的一个点，直到看见真实照片，才明白那里的人每天怎么跟寒冷相处。

example_translations.translation: When the lesson turned to the North Pole, the teacher did not start with a map; she first asked everyone what life would become if you could not see the sun for half a year.
The video section about Arctic fieldwork was filmed so quietly, with only the wind and the sound underfoot, yet people still could not look away.
As a child, he always thought the North Pole was just a dot in a textbook, and only after seeing real photos did he understand how people there live with the cold every day.

glosses.notes: The continent of North America.

examples.sentence: 博物馆新开的展览把北美洲不同地区的移民故事放在一起看，很多观众一圈走完都说收获特别大。
公司准备把这款服务先放到北美洲试用，不是因为别的市场不重要，而是那边的反馈速度通常更快。
她原本只在书里看过北美洲的地形介绍，真正坐飞机从上空望下去时，才第一次感觉到那片地方有多大。

example_translations.translation: The museum's new exhibition sets immigration stories from different parts of North America side by side, and many visitors say they learned a great deal after walking through it.
The company plans to roll out this service in North America first, not because other markets do not matter, but because feedback there usually comes faster.
She had only read about North America's terrain in books; only when she looked down from a plane did she feel for the first time how vast that place really is.

glosses.notes: Describes being passive or forced to react instead of taking the initiative.

examples.sentence: 客服如果每次都等用户生气了再解释，就一直会很被动，因为对方最想听的话往往已经错过了时机。
他在讨论里不是没有想法，只是总怕说错，于是越沉默越被动，最后连本来熟悉的部分也不敢接。
暴雨来的时候，景区只靠现场广播通知游客实在太被动，所以后来又加了手机提醒和路口引导。

example_translations.translation: If customer service waits until users are already angry before explaining things, it will always stay passive, because the moment when the other side most wanted to hear those words has usually already passed.

It is not that he had no ideas in the discussion; he was just afraid of saying the wrong thing, so the more silent he became, the more passive he became, and in the end he did not even dare take on the parts he knew well.
When the storm hit, it was too passive for the scenic area to rely only on loudspeaker announcements, so later they added phone alerts and guidance at intersections.

glosses.notes: Used when someone has no real choice and must do something because of pressure or circumstances.

examples.sentence: 临时改签以后，他们被迫在路上的城市住了一晚，行李没跟上，第二天开会时每个人都显得特别累。
那家小店原本还能撑下去，房租和原料一起涨得太快，老板最后还是被迫把营业时间缩短了一半。
由于上游道路突然封闭，送药的车队被迫改走山路，多花了三个多小时才赶到镇上的医院。

example_translations.translation: After a last-minute rebooking, they were forced to spend a night in a city on the way. Their luggage did not catch up, and everyone looked especially tired at the meeting the next day.
That small shop might have held on, but with rent and raw materials rising too quickly together, the owner was still forced to cut business hours in half.
Because the upstream road was suddenly closed, the medicine convoy was forced to take the mountain route, arriving at the town hospital more than three hours later.

glosses.notes: A sleeveless top, often worn as an undershirt or in hot weather.

examples.sentence: 天热得厉害，搬货的师傅只穿一件背心就在仓库里来回跑，脸上的汗还是不停往下掉。
朋友临时拉他去打球，他连外套都没来得及换，只好穿着里面的白背心直接上场，结果反而跑得最卖力。
夜市卖衣服的老板把几种颜色的背心一排挂在灯下，让路过的人一眼就能看出布料的薄厚。

example_translations.translation: It was so hot that the delivery worker kept running back and forth through the warehouse in only a sleeveless undershirt, yet sweat still kept pouring down his face.

A friend pulled him off to play ball at the last minute, and he did not even have time to change, so he had to go straight onto the court in the white vest he was wearing underneath, and ended up running the hardest.
The clothing seller at the night market hung several colors of vests in a row under the lights so passersby could tell the thickness of the fabric at a glance.

glosses.notes: Used for something prepared in advance so it can be used if the main option fails.

examples.sentence: 前台怕周末突然停电，早就把一个备用电源放在后院，连线路都提前检查过一遍。
她出远门时总会在包里放一副备用眼镜，因为上次眼镜半路坏了以后，整趟行程都被打乱了。
演出开始前，大家又把一台电脑放在旁边备用，免得前面那台一出问题，全场的人只能干等。

example_translations.translation: Worried about a weekend power outage, the front desk had already placed a backup power supply in the back yard and checked all the wiring in advance.
Whenever she travels far, she keeps a backup pair of glasses in her bag, because the last time her glasses broke halfway through the trip, the whole journey was thrown into disorder.
Before the show started, they put another computer at the side as a backup so that if the front one failed, everyone in the room would not be left waiting.

glosses.notes: Used when an amount or effect increases dramatically, often to twice the previous level or more.

examples.sentence: 新路线开通以后，从城南到机场开车的时间一下缩短了很多，周围几家旅馆周末的订单也跟着倍增。
老店把收银和点单系统一起换掉以后，忙的时候虽然客人更多了，出错的压力没有像以前那样倍增。
这部纪录片播出以后，小镇的游客数量在一个月里倍增，连平时最安静的老街都开始排队。

example_translations.translation: After the new route opened, the driving time from the south side of the city to the airport dropped sharply, and weekend bookings at several nearby hotels doubled as well.
After the old shop replaced both its checkout and ordering systems, there were more customers during busy hours, but the pressure of making mistakes did not multiply the way it used to.
After the documentary aired, visitor numbers in the small town doubled within a month, and even the old street that used to be quiet started to have lines.

glosses.notes: Used for running on foot with visible speed or energy.

examples.sentence: 比赛还没正式开始，看台边那个小朋友就已经穿着大一号的运动鞋来回奔跑，像是把全场气氛都带热了。
听见身后有人喊停下，她没有回头，只是继续沿着河边的小路奔跑，直到看见桥下那家亮着灯的小店。
山里的雨说来就来，带队的人一喊，原本分散拍照的游客都背着包往停车场方向奔跑起来。

example_translations.translation: Before the match had even officially started, the little kid by the stands was already running back and forth in oversized sneakers, as if warming up the whole place by himself.
When she heard someone behind her shouting for her to stop, she did not turn back; she kept running along the small path by the river until she saw the lit shop under the bridge.
Mountain rain comes suddenly, and the moment the guide shouted, the visitors who had been scattered taking photos all started running toward the parking area with their bags.

glosses.notes: Can mean the inborn instinct itself or, in phrases like 本能地, acting by instinct.

examples.sentence: 孩子看见杯子快滑下去的时候，一下就本能地伸手一接，连旁边的大人都没反应过来。
大家一听见响声，虽然还不知道发生了什么，却还是本能地先去找最近的出口，这比站着猜原因有用得多。
她做记者很多年了，一听见对方突然停顿，就会本能地追问前面那句话背后没说完的部分。

example_translations.translation: When the child saw the cup about to slide off, he instinctively shot out a hand and caught it before the adults nearby had even reacted.
The moment everyone heard the sound, even before they knew what had happened, they still instinctively looked for the nearest exit; that was far more useful than standing there guessing why.
She has worked as a reporter for many years, and whenever the other person suddenly pauses, she instinctively follows up on the unfinished part behind the previous sentence.

glosses.notes: Points back to the thing itself, often to separate its nature from outside influences or added factors.

examples.sentence: 这份工作本身并不轻松，难的是你得一边面对不停变化的安排，一边还要让每个人都觉得被照顾到了。
大家后来发现，问题不在规则本身，而在执行的时候有人总想图快，结果把原来简单的事越弄越复杂。
旅行最让她着迷的不是打卡多少地方，而是路上那些计划本身以外的变化，常常反而留下更深的印象。

example_translations.translation: The job itself is not easy; the hard part is that you have to face constantly changing arrangements while still making everyone feel looked after.

People later realized that the problem was not in the rules themselves, but in the fact that someone always wanted speed during execution, turning something simple into something more and more complicated.
What fascinates her most about travel is not how many places she checks off, but the changes outside the plan itself that happen on the road, which often leave a deeper impression.

glosses.notes: Refers to the local country or area, and by extension things that belong to it or developed there.

examples.sentence: 新开的展览没有只介绍国际品牌，反而把很多年轻人做的本土作品放在最显眼的位置。
那家小店想吸引游客，真正让它慢慢做下去的，还是周围的人对本土口味点心的长期支持。
球队换了教练以后，开始更重视本土年轻队员的培养，因为俱乐部不想一直靠外面临时买人。

example_translations.translation: The new exhibition did not only introduce international brands; instead, it placed many local works made by young people in the most prominent spots.
The small shop wanted to attract tourists, but what really kept it going little by little was the long-term support of the people around it for local-flavor pastries.
After the team changed coaches, it started paying more attention to training local young players, because the club did not want to keep buying people from outside at the last minute.

glosses.notes: Used when pressure drives someone or something into a decision, action, or state.

examples.sentence: 截止时间一下逼到眼前，大家才发现前面拖着不做的小问题已经堆成大麻烦。
他不是想大声逼别人同意自己，而是怕如果今天还定不下来，后面的安排都会一起乱掉。
连着几天的高温把仓库里的水果逼得熟得太快，负责人只好临时联系更多车辆连夜送走。

example_translations.translation: When the deadline suddenly pressed right up against them, everyone realized that the small problems they had kept putting off had already piled up into one big mess.
He was not trying to force others to agree with him by speaking loudly; he was afraid that if they still could not settle it today, everything scheduled afterward would fall into disorder.
Several days of high heat forced the fruit in the warehouse to ripen too quickly, so the person in charge had to contact more vehicles and send it out overnight.

glosses.notes: Often means to compare one thing to another as an analogy to make an idea easier to grasp.

examples.sentence: 老师讲抽象概念的时候，总爱把看不见的压力比方成背上的大包，这样学生一下就懂了。
她没有直接批评对方，只是把这种合作关系比方成一根太松的线，意思已经说得很清楚了。
记者在节目里把城市更新比方成给老房子一点一点换掉坏掉的部分，听众一下就明白工程为什么那么慢。

example_translations.translation: When the teacher explains abstract concepts, she likes to liken invisible pressure to a large bag on someone's back, and the students understand at once.
She did not criticize the other side directly; she only compared this working relationship to a line tied too loosely, and her point was already very clear.
On the program, the reporter likened urban renewal to slowly replacing the worn-out parts of an old house bit by bit, and the audience immediately understood why the project moved so slowly.

glosses.notes: The relative share or weight something takes up in a total.

examples.sentence: 今年计划里留给基础维护的比重明显提高了，因为大家终于意识到，老问题拖得越久，后面花的钱只会更多。
在这份调查里，三十岁以下用户的意见占的比重并不低，所以团队最后没有按老办法直接做决定。
导演后期剪片时特意降低了配乐的比重，想让观众更多听见街上的声音和人物真实的呼吸。

example_translations.translation: This year the proportion set aside for basic maintenance in the plan rose noticeably, because everyone finally realized that the longer old problems drag on, the more money will be spent later.
In this survey, the share of opinions from users under thirty was not small, so the team did not use the old method to make its decision in the end.
While editing the film, the director intentionally reduced the proportion of background music, hoping viewers would hear more of the street sounds and the characters' real breathing.
